Estimator's noteShort moves are usually billed by the hour for the crew and truck. Long moves are priced by the weight of your things and the distance. Your ZIP codes decide which applies.

The cheapest long distance moving options are the ones where you do the work: a one-way rental truck you load and drive, at typical published rates of $1.00–$2.00 per road mile with fuel extra, or a portable container that a company drives for you. Full-service movers cost the most. They charge $2,600–$5,700 for a 2-bedroom home over 1,000 road miles, on an off-peak date with no stairs or add-ons.

The cheapest long distance moving options, from least to most

Put in order of what they usually cost for a whole home, the cheapest long distance moving options run from doing everything yourself to paying a company to do it all. Each step down this list trades some of your time and effort for money.

  1. Take less, and ship only what matters. Selling or giving away furniture before a long move cuts every other cost on this list. Movers price a handful of pieces on their own: 4 to 10 items cost $820–$2,450 over 1,000 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or add-ons.
  2. A trailer behind your own car. For a studio or a light load, a cargo trailer saves renting a truck, as long as your car has a hitch rated for the weight.
  3. A one-way rental truck. You load, drive and unload. For a whole home, this is the best known of the cheapest long distance moving options: billed by the road mile, with fuel extra, and with a set number of days to make the trip.
  4. A rental truck with hired loading help. You drive, and a labor-only crew lifts at each end. Two movers to load cost $200–$520 and two to unload cost $200–$460, off peak, with no truck included.
  5. A portable container or a freight trailer. You pack and load, and the company drives. Published figures put each delivery, transfer or pickup trip at $74.99–$150.00, and the company quotes the long haul by route and by how much space you fill.
  6. Full-service movers. A crew loads, drives and unloads, and packs too if you pay for it. This is the dearest of the cheapest long distance moving options, but it is the only one that asks nothing of you.

The order isn't fixed. Fuel, tolls and nights in a motel add to a truck's rate, and a small load can cost little with a container or with movers. Price the cheapest long distance moving options on your own route, with the calculator above, before you rule any of them out.

What each choice leaves for you to do

Every one of the cheapest long distance moving options has a low price on paper and some work behind it. With a rental truck, you pack every box, carry every piece of furniture and drive a large vehicle for several days. You also pay for fuel, tolls, meals and motels, and you may want the rental company's damage cover for the truck. Count the days off work too.

A container or freight trailer takes the driving off you, but you still pack and load it. The container also needs somewhere legal to sit while you fill it: a driveway, or a street space that may need a city permit. Full-service movers take on all of the work, but you give up some control of the date: long-distance movers usually give a delivery window of several days rather than a set day.

Weigh those trade-offs against the prices of the cheapest long distance moving options. If driving a 26 ft truck through several states isn't something you would do, the savings of a self-drive move don't apply to you.

Matching the cheapest long distance moving options to your home

How much you own decides which of the cheapest long distance moving options comes out lowest for you. As a rough guide, by home size:

  • A dorm room or a few boxes: pack your car, send boxes by ground freight or a parcel service, or ask movers for a few-items price. Moving 1 to 3 items costs $610–$1,400 at 1,000 road miles, off peak.
  • A studio or 1-bedroom: a container or a small truck is usually the low-cost pick. Movers charge $1,400–$3,300 for a 1-bedroom home on the same terms, so price both before you choose.
  • 2 or 3 bedrooms: a rental truck with hired loading help often costs least, if you're willing to drive it. A container move may need two units.
  • 4 or more bedrooms: one rental truck may not hold it all, and the largest trucks are hard work over long distances. Get written estimates from movers as well as truck and container prices.

Hybrid moves: pay only for the hard part

You don't have to pick just one. Many of the cheapest long distance moving options work best when you mix them, paying for help only where your own effort runs out:

  • Rent a truck, and hire labor only to load and unload it. A crew of 2 for loading and unloading costs $320–$910 on a local job, so on a long move price a crew at each end.
  • Book a container, and pay a crew for a few hours to load it, so you only do the driving to the new home.
  • Hire movers for the heavy pieces, such as a sofa, appliances or a piano, and take the boxes yourself.
  • Pack your own boxes and let full-service movers do the rest, which takes the packing charge off the bill.

Checks before you book a low price

The lowest figure among the cheapest long distance moving options only counts if it holds on delivery day. Before you pay a deposit:

  • Find out who will move your things. A broker sells your move and hands it to a mover; it doesn't own trucks. Look up the USDOT number of the company that will actually carry your goods across state lines with FMCSA.
  • Get a written estimate after a survey. The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration lists an estimate given by phone or online, sight unseen, as a red flag, along with a demand for cash or a large deposit before the move. See FMCSA's red flags.
  • Ask whether the estimate is binding. With a binding estimate, you pay no more than its amount at delivery for the services it lists. FMCSA explains binding estimates.
  • Read the rental or container contract. Check the days and miles included, the fee for extra days, and what the damage cover leaves out.

Choosing among the cheapest long distance moving options

To compare the cheapest long distance moving options fairly, price each one for the same home, the same route and the same dates:

  1. Enter your ZIP codes in the calculator above. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to show the range for full-service movers.
  2. Price a one-way truck and a container for the same dates, and add fuel, lodging and days off work to the truck.
  3. Ask at least three movers for written estimates after a video or in-home survey.
  4. Set the totals side by side, with the work each one leaves to you.

The best of the cheapest long distance moving options is the one whose full cost, your own time included, comes out lowest for your home and your route.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • A 2-bedroom home move takes up about 640–930 cu ft: the smallest truck that holds the heavy end is 20 ft.
  • With 3 movers, a 2-bedroom home move takes about 4–6.5 hours on site: $720–$1,800 off peak at 10 road miles.
  • Tip guides suggest $40–$100 per mover for each working day, to each crew: $40–$100 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $120–$300 for 3 movers.
  • A 2-bedroom home move of 1,000 road miles, off peak: $1,340–$2,610 with a rental truck before help, and $2,600–$5,700 with full-service movers.
  • Over 1,000 road miles, a typical 2-bedroom home of about 6,000 lb has a trucking charge of $2,200–$3,300 off peak, before loading, unloading and the first 50 miles.
  • Guides put a 2-bedroom home at about 40–90 boxes.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 8 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • A move across a state line is an interstate move, so the federal rules for household goods movers apply.
  • Released value pays at most 60 cents a pound: $36 for your 60 lb TV worth $400, against up to $400 with full-value protection.
  • Loading and driving a truck yourself is usually the lowest-cost way to move a whole home a long way, but it costs you days on the road.
  • A portable container or freight trailer splits the work: you pack and load, and a company does the driving.
  • Hiring labor only at each end of a rental truck move keeps the cost far below full service and spares your back.
  • Check a company's USDOT number with FMCSA, and whether it is a broker, before you pay a deposit.

Tips for loaders and long-haul crews

Tips never show up in a quote for the cheapest long distance moving options, so set them aside. Work out what guides suggest for each mover, by the hour, by the day or as a share of the bill.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $40–$100

For the crew $120–$300

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

Booking steps from first quote to delivery

Whichever of the cheapest long distance moving options you choose, a missed step costs money later. Tick off these tasks, from comparing three estimates to filing a claim, and enter your date to see when each is due.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Before an interstate move, movers are required to give you FMCSA's booklet Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move and its Ready to Move brochure.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

  • Give each one the same details, so the prices compare like for like.

6 weeks before

  • On an interstate move, a binding estimate means you don't have to pay more than the estimated amount at delivery; added items or services, or something unforeseen such as stairs or a parking permit, call for a new binding estimate. Under a non-binding one, the mover can't require more than 110 percent of the estimate at delivery.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

  • Moving hours, elevators, loading docks and gates. If one wants the company's certificate of insurance, ask the company to send it ahead.

  • Then compare it with the coverage the moving company offers.

  • Interstate movers must be registered with FMCSA: make sure yours has a U.S. DOT number. FMCSA's database of registered movers also shows insurance and complaint records.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

4 weeks before

  • Whether it takes a deposit, when the rest is due, and which payment methods it accepts.

2 weeks before

  • Get a name and a direct number, not only the main office line.

  • Aim to reach the new home before the truck does.

1 week before

  • Make sure someone can be at the new home on every day of the window.

Moving day

  • On an interstate move, the mover must prepare an inventory of your things, and you both sign each page of it. You should get a partly completed copy of the bill of lading before the mover leaves your old home.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

  • Photograph each page if no copy is handed to you.

After the move

  • After an interstate move, FMCSA says you have 9 months from the date of delivery to file it. List what's missing or damaged, and add photos.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

  • If you're on active duty in the Armed Forces and moved under a military order for a permanent change of station, the IRS says you may be able to deduct moving costs you weren't reimbursed for.

    Source: Internal Revenue Service

Federal protections when a mover crosses state lines

If your pick among the cheapest long distance moving options is a mover crossing a state line, federal rules apply. These cover the paperwork, delays, disputes and the basic cover the price includes.

  1. The mover must have an arbitration program

    The mover must have an arbitration program for disputes about loss or damage, and about charges beyond those collected at delivery. It must tell you about it before the bill of lading, can't make you agree to arbitration before a dispute arises, and can't charge you more than half the cost of starting it.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.211 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  2. The delivery receipt can't contain a release of liability

    Your delivery receipt must not contain any wording that claims to release the mover or its agents from liability. It may say the goods arrived in apparent good condition, except as noted.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.701 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  3. You get the bill of lading at least 3 days before loading

    The bill of lading must be given to you, and signed and dated by you, at least 3 days before the shipment is scheduled to be loaded. For 3 days after you sign it, you may cancel it without penalty.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.505 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  4. A late pickup or delivery means a notice

    If the mover can't pick up or deliver on the dates in the bill of lading, it must tell you as soon as the delay becomes apparent, at its own expense, and give you the dates it expects instead. It must keep a written record, and give you a copy if you ask.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.605 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  5. Released Value pays by weight, not by worth

    Released Value Protection costs nothing extra, but the mover is responsible for no more than 60 cents per pound per article. Under federal rules, that limit comes from the Surface Transportation Board's released rates order, and a mover may raise the rate each year in line with the U.S. Department of Commerce's cost of living adjustment. You get it only by signing a statement on the bill of lading or contract agreeing to it.

    Source: FMCSA, Liability & Protection (fmcsa.dot.gov, read 2026-10-28); 49 CFR 375.201 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

More on these rules from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration: Protect Your Move.

What the free basic cover actually pays

Hiring a mover, the dearest of the cheapest long distance moving options, includes basic released value cover at no charge. Enter an item's weight and worth to see what it pays against full-value protection.

If your $400 TV is broken, basic cover pays $36.

Released value, the basic cover a mover includes at no charge, pays at most 60 cents a pound for each item. Full-value protection pays to repair or replace it, up to its value. The released rate is the Surface Transportation Board's, and a mover may raise it each year. Full-value protection is the default: a mover's estimate must include it, and your goods move under it unless you give it up in writing. Under it, a mover may pay at most $100 a pound for an item worth more than $100 a pound, such as jewelry, unless you list the item in writing.

Released value pays $36

Full-value protection pays up to $400

Full-value protection is priced on the whole shipment: about $10.00–$20.00 per $1,000 of declared value.

Questions

What are the cheapest long distance moving options? FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

Are moving containers cheaper than a rental truck?

It depends on what you add to the truck. A one-way truck's rate leaves out fuel, motels and days of driving, while a container's price covers the long haul and leaves you the packing and loading. Published figures put each container delivery or pickup trip at $74.99–$150.00. Of the cheapest long distance moving options, total both for your route before you decide.

Are there alternatives to U-Haul for a one-way move?

Yes. Other national truck rental companies, such as Penske and Budget, rent one-way trucks, and container and freight-trailer companies offer a self-pack move without the driving. Getting a price from more than one of them is a simple way to find the cheapest long distance moving options for your dates, since one-way rates vary by route and season.

When is a rental truck not one of the cheapest long distance moving options?

When your load needs two trucks, or the largest size, which is hard work to drive for days. It also loses when fuel, motels, meals and time off work add up to more than a container or a small move with movers. More than 10 items with movers cost $1,650–$4,550 at 1,000 road miles, off peak, so price that against the truck.

Are long-distance moving companies that aren't brokers cheaper?

Not always. A broker sells your move and passes it to a mover, while a mover, the carrier, does the work itself. Either way, check the USDOT number of the company that will carry your goods and get its written estimate, so you know who answers for the price.
